stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Pinned-source conventions: work over the big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. A category fibred in groupoids is represented by an algebraic space $F$ over $S$ if it is equivalent over the site to $\mathcal S_F$, the category fibred in sets associated to the functor of points of $F$. A fibred category is fibred in setoids when its fibre categories are groupoids and all their objects have trivial automorphism groups. For a presheaf $F$ of sets, $\mathcal S_F$ is its associated category fibred in sets: its objects over $T$ are elements of $F(T)$. A 1-morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ of categories fibred in groupoids is representable by algebraic spaces when for EVERY scheme $U$ over $S$ and every $y\in\mathcal Y_U$, the 2-fibre product $(\Sch/U)_{fppf}\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$ is represented by an algebraic space over $U$.
For a map $a:F\to G$ of presheaves of sets, the separate Bootstrap definition says that $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces when for EVERY scheme $U$ over $S$ and EVERY section $\xi\in G(U)$, the presheaf fibre product $h_U\times_{G,\xi}F$ is represented by an algebraic space over $U$; here $h_U$ is the presheaf of points of $U$.
For a property $\mathcal P$ of morphisms of algebraic spaces, assume (i) $\mathcal P$ is preserved by arbitrary base changes and (ii) $\mathcal P$ is fppf local on the TARGET (base of a representing morphism). A morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ represented by algebraic spaces has $\mathcal P$ when for every $U$ and $y\in\mathcal Y_U$, the induced morphism $F_y\to U$ has $\mathcal P$. The Bootstrap definition for a representable morphism of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is parallel: $a$ has $\mathcal P$ iff for EVERY $U$ and $\xi\in G(U)$ the representing algebraic-space map $(h_U\times_G F)\to U$ has $\mathcal P$.

Let $a:F\to G$ be a morphism of presheaves of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ that is representable by algebraic spaces, and let $\mathcal P$ be a property of algebraic-space morphisms stable under arbitrary base change and fppf local on the target. The map $a$ has property $\mathcal P$ in the presheaf sense if and only if the induced $1$-morphism $\mathcal S_F\to\mathcal S_G$ has property $\mathcal P$ in the represented-fibred-category sense.

A $1$-morphism $f:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is representable by algebraic spaces when for every $U\to S$ and $y\in\mathcal Y_U$, the $2$-fibre product of $\mathcal X$ with $(\Sch/U)_{fppf}$ over $y:\,(\Sch/U)_{fppf}\to\mathcal Y$ is represented by an algebraic space $F_y$ over $U$. A property $\mathcal P$ in this section is a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces, invariant under EVERY base change and fppf local on the TARGET. A representable $f$ has property $\mathcal P$ when each induced morphism $F_y\to U$ has $\mathcal P$. Two fibre-product squares are interpreted 2-categorically.

Let $\mathcal{X}, \mathcal{Y}, \mathcal{Z}$

\xymatrix{

\mathcal{X} \ar[d]^f \\
\mathcal{Z} \ar[r]^g & \mathcal{Y}
}
$$
If $f$ has $\mathcal{P}$, then the base change $f'$
has $\mathcal{P}$.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Work over the big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. A category fibred in groupoids is represented by an algebraic space when it is equivalent to the fibred category of points of an algebraic space over $S$. A 1-morphism of fibred categories is representable by algebraic spaces if every 2-base change by a morphism from a scheme is represented by an algebraic space. A representable morphism $j:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is a monomorphism when each induced morphism $F_y\to U$ of algebraic spaces is a monomorphism, i.e., its diagonal is an isomorphism.

Let $j:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a 1-morphism of categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Suppose that $j$ is representable by algebraic spaces and, for every scheme $U/S$ and $y\in\mathcal Y_U$, its represented base change $F_y\to U$ is a monomorphism of algebraic spaces. Then for every scheme $U/S$ the functor $j_U:\mathcal X_U\to\mathcal Y_U$ is fully faithful.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Work over the big fppf site $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. A category fibred in groupoids is represented by an algebraic space when it is equivalent to the fibred category of points of an algebraic space over $S$. A 1-morphism of fibred categories is representable by algebraic spaces if every 2-base change by a morphism from a scheme is represented by an algebraic space. A representable morphism $j:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ is a monomorphism when each induced morphism $F_y\to U$ of algebraic spaces is a monomorphism, i.e., its diagonal is an isomorphism. For any $U/S$ and objects $x,y\in\mathcal X_U$, $\mathit{Isom}(x,y)$ denotes the functor on schemes $V\to U$ of isomorphisms between pullbacks of $x$ and $y$. The diagonal $\Delta_\mathcal X:\mathcal X\to\mathcal X\times_{(\Sch/S)_{fppf}}\mathcal X$ sends each object to the pair $(x,x)$. A representable category fibred in groupoids means one equivalent to $(\Sch/U)_{fppf}$ for a scheme $U/S$; representable by an algebraic space is a broader condition. All products of fibred categories are 2-products.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a category fibred in groupoids over
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the diagonal $\mathcal{X} \to \mathcal{X} \times \mathcal{X}$
is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every scheme $U$ over $S$, and any
$x, y \in \Ob(\mathcal{X}_U)$ the sheaf
$\mathit{Isom}(x, y)$ is an algebraic space over $U$,
\item for every scheme $U$ over $S$, and any $x \in \Ob(\mathcal{X}_U)$
the associated $1$-morphism $x : (\Sch/U)_{fppf} \to \mathcal{X}$
is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every pair of schemes $T_1, T_2$ over $S$, and any
$x_i \in \Ob(\mathcal{X}_{T_i})$, $i = 1, 2$ the $2$-fibre product
$(\Sch/T_1)_{fppf} \times_{x_1, \mathcal{X}, x_2}
(\Sch/T_2)_{fppf}$
is representable by an algebraic space,
\item for every representable category fibred in groupoids $\mathcal{U}$
over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ every $1$-morphism
$\mathcal{U} \to \mathcal{X}$ is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every pair $\mathcal{T}_1, \mathcal{T}_2$ of representable
categories fibred in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ and any
$1$-morphisms $x_i : \mathcal{T}_i \to \mathcal{X}$, $i = 1, 2$ the
$2$-fibre product $\mathcal{T}_1 \times_{x_1, \mathcal{X}, x_2} \mathcal{T}_2$
is representable by an algebraic space,
\item for every category fibred in groupoids $\mathcal{U}$
over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ which is
representable by an algebraic space every $1$-morphism
$\mathcal{U} \to \mathcal{X}$ is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every pair $\mathcal{T}_1, \mathcal{T}_2$ of categories fibred
in groupoids over $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ which are representable
by algebraic spaces, and any $1$-morphisms
$x_i : \mathcal{T}_i \to \mathcal{X}$ the
$2$-fibre product $\mathcal{T}_1 \times_{x_1, \mathcal{X}, x_2} \mathcal{T}_2$
is representable by an algebraic space.
\end{enumerate}
